Here are concise steps you can follow (Photoshop, GIMP, or mobile) to remove the mug while leaving everything else unchanged:

Photoshop (quick):
1. Duplicate the Background layer.
2. Use Lasso or Pen to roughly select the mug and a small surrounding area.
3. Edit > Content-Aware Fill (or Edit > Fill > Content-Aware). Accept the preview and apply.
4. Use the Spot Healing Brush or Clone Stamp to clean edges and restore any fine texture or shadow continuity.
5. Zoom in and refine with the Clone Stamp/Healing Brush on tight edges near the product.
6. Flatten and save a copy.

GIMP (free):
1. Duplicate the layer.
2. Use the Free Select or Paths tool to select the mug area.
3. Use Filters > Enhance > Heal Selection (or manually use the Clone tool) to fill the selection using surrounding pixels.
4. Use the Clone/Heal tools to fix remaining artifacts and restore shadows/details.
5. Export the edited image.

Mobile (Snapseed):
1. Open image > Tools > Healing.
2. Zoom in and paint over the mug in small strokes; undo any bad strokes.
3. Finish and export.

Tips to preserve the product:
- Work on a duplicated layer so you can revert.
- Sample nearby background and shadow areas when cloning to maintain consistent lighting and texture.
- Fix fine edges around the product last, using a small brush size and subtle cloning/healing.

If you prefer, you can upload the image to an online retouching service or ask a photo editor to do a professional removal.
